title: Reading Camera Settings in Plain Terms
excerpt: Every Gallery photo records its camera and exposure. Here is what those numbers mean and how they shaped a few frames.
author: Mono Chromattic
imageCaption: A koi, photographed at f/5.6, 1/200 s and ISO 640.
content:
## What the lightbox shows

Open any photo in the Gallery and the info panel lists **camera, lens, aperture, shutter, ISO and focal length**. Together they describe how a picture was made.

- **Aperture** (f/number) controls depth of field. Lower numbers blur the background more.
- **Shutter** speed controls motion. 1/1000 s freezes a bird; 1/30 s lets lights streak.
- **ISO** is sensor sensitivity. Higher means brighter but noisier.
- **Focal length** sets the field of view.

### Three examples

| Photo | Aperture | Shutter | ISO |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Koi in Still Water | f/5.6 | 1/200 s | 640 |
| Torii in Autumn | f/4 | 1/50 s | 800 |
| Tokyo Skytree After Dark | f/2.8 | 1/30 s | 1600 |
